result.title: GARP: Real-Time Generative Agents on Local Hardware in a Game Engine
result.summary: Generative agents are game characters whose plans, conversations, and memories are written on the fly by a large language model (LLM). The original Generative Agents demonstration used cloud inference in a custom simulation. We present GARP, a platform for real-time generative agents inside Godot, and describe the Character Behavior System used in GARP 2. The complete loop runs on local hardware using a 3B-parameter open-weight model and no cloud service. Alongside the original planning, memory, and reflection, GARP gives each agent an emotion system driven by LLM appraisal, four graded personality axes drawn from the Big Five that set simulation parameters as well as prompt text, six needs whose urgency grows over time, and pairwise relationships updated after every conversation. The system narrows 50+ candidate actions to typically 3-8, constrains model responses with JSON schemas, and surfaces important memories in decision prompts. A layered optimization strategy (an adjustable game clock, decisions taken ahead of need, multi-tier caching, prompt compression, and fully asynchronous execution) keeps the game responsive while the model thinks. In a nine-scenario evaluation, 25 of 27 runs passed log-based checks. Both failures occurred in the birthday party scenario, where one guest omitted the event from their daily plan.

AI.brief_summary: GARP 是在 Godot 引擎内用本地 3B 开源模型驱动实时生成式游戏智能体的平台，在规划、记忆与反思之外加入情绪、人格、需求与关系状态，并以动作候选收窄、JSON 约束、分层缓存和全异步执行维持响应。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「记忆浮现到决策提示—候选动作从 50+ 收窄到 3-8—预决策与多级缓存」的调度思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的延迟成本权衡；但该工作无视觉输入也无 latent 表示，联系较远。
